extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs and policy
extracted.subtask_description: A mid-20th-century newspaper report covering international diplomacy, United Nations procedure, and multilateral policy proposals (e.g., FAO food-distribution plan). Intended as a contemporaneous news account rather than a how-to guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Council document submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents for Security Council consideration must be submitted according to the Council's rule requiring three days' lead time for submission before debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft agreements and their lengthy appendices need to be delivered within this time frame so members can study them; if key documents/appendices are not yet delivered the Council may agree to delay the debate for several days until they are ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair enforcement of decorum in UN debates
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding chair will not permit undignified language or personal name-calling during debates and will order such statements expunged from the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prohibited expressions include epithets like 'satellite of Moscow' or other insults; delegates should avoid inflammatory rhetoric or risk censure and removal of remarks from official records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification process for transfer-of-sovereignty agreements (Hague pact / Indonesia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The transfer agreement must be approved by multiple bodies: the Indonesian Republican Parliament, the Netherlands Parliament, and the fifteen Dutch-sponsored federalist states in Indonesia; the Republican Parliament will be convened to vote (reported not later than Dec. 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratification in most of the Dutch-sponsored federalist states is expected to be largely a formality, but formal approvals across metropolitan and local entities are required before the transfer is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Council acceptance / veto risk for reports and membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Security Council can reject reports on agreements and permanent members (e.g., Russia) theoretically can exercise a veto that could delay or block acceptance of reports or applications (such as UN membership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with working agreements, political opposition by a permanent member may delay ratification or admission processes; sponsors should anticipate diplomatic maneuvering and potential abstentions or vetoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: World food bank / clearing-house operational principles (FAO proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAO-proposed world food bank would buy and sell surplus commodities offered by producing areas, transacting either at special cut-rate prices or at regular commercial prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the proposal, countries able to pay in acceptable/convertible currencies would obtain supplies at regular prices, while payments in unconvertible currency would be accepted at special prices and credited to producing countries' accounts. The plan envisions significant capital (reported example: $5,000,000,000) contributed by participating nations and must avoid functioning de facto as another loan program that increases recipient indebtedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAO benchmark: food production vs. population growth
rubrics_metrics.description: To raise world living standards, food production must increase faster than population growth; current evidence shows food production is not expanding at the necessary rate in many regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing this requires technical aid to increase production in underdeveloped areas and resolving distribution/currency barriers so surpluses can reach shortage areas; policy choices (e.g., crop controls, export restrictions) and financing mechanisms will affect outcomes.
